ideas: What you bought and why you wanted it
What went wrong after buying it
What the experience taught you about shopping

phrases.meaning: stay unused for a long time

model: The thing I regret buying most is an expensive smart exercise bike that I ordered online about two years ago. It was a complete impulse buy. It was the middle of the pandemic, the gyms were closed, and one night I saw an advert on social media for a flash sale. The bike had a big touch screen and came with a year of free online classes, and the price was forty percent off. It seemed too good to be true, but I fell for it and paid in about five minutes. When the bike arrived, the first problem was the size. My apartment was quite small, and the bike took up almost half of the living room. Then I discovered that the free classes were only in English and Chinese, and after the first year you had to pay a monthly fee. I used it every day for the first couple of weeks, but when the gyms opened again, I went back to running outside. For over a year it just sat in the corner gathering dust, and I actually hung my laundry on it. I felt terrible buyer's remorse, because it was a waste of money that I'd been saving for a trip. In the end I sold it to a neighbour for about a third of the price. Now, whenever I see an amazing deal online, I think twice and wait at least a day.
